rounds.text: Narmada Gelatines Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a P/E ratio of 10.7x and a price-to-book ratio of 2.15x [E1, E2], while offering a dividend yield of 2.18% [E4]. The business demonstrates elite capital efficiency, boasting an ROCE of 27.9% and an ROE of 21.8% [E6, E7]. Operational profitability is surging, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 72% [E15] and a yearly operating margin reaching 19% in March 2026, which is an expansion of 9 percentage points over three years [E24]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x and total borrowings reduced to ₹ 8 Cr [E32, E33, E53], backed by ₹ 15 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E30]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 9.82% over the past five years [E56]. Operating within a sector experiencing a tailwind score of +0.77 [E63], the rules-based screen awards the setup a strong score of 93 out of 100 [E57].

While recent profit growth looks impressive, the underlying top-line expansion paints a much slower picture with 3-year compounded sales growth at a meager 4% [E10] and a poor 5-year sales growth rate of 9.82% [E56]. Volume headwinds are already visible as annual report disclosures confirm that sales volumes for both gelatine and DCP declined by 5% and 8% respectively [E76]. The structural growth profile of the core industry is also highly constrained, with India's gelatin market projected to crawl at an annual CAGR of only 2 to 3% over the next few years [E69]. Operational risks threaten the sustainability of recent margin gains, notably because the availability of the primary raw material—crushed bones—remains a persistent cause for concern and a major sourcing issue [E78]. Furthermore, the company faces severe competitive threats from unscrupulous traders importing low-cost industrial-grade gelatin from China, which is sometimes illicitly blended with high-quality domestic product [E79], alongside the primary market barrier posed by the rise of plant-based gelatin substitutes [E77]. These operational vulnerabilities are compounded by insider dilution, with promoter holding having drifted downward from 77.65% in September 2023 to 75.00% by June 2026 [E35]. Investors chasing recent momentum also face extreme historical volatility of 56.7% [E47] and a devastating worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -81.5% [E46]. Conceded: [E38]

Conceded: [E10], [E56], [E76], [E78], [E79], [E77], [E35], [E47], [E46]. While top-line growth metrics appear moderate, the company's profitability and capital efficiency tell a vastly superior story, with 5-year compounded profit growth at an exceptional 39% [E13] and trailing twelve-month profit growth surging by 72% [E15]. Operating margins have climbed impressively to 19% against 10% three years prior [E24], supported by improved boiler efficiency and lower coal consumption [E73], proving that operational quality and margin expansion far outweigh raw sales volume metrics. The valuation remains deeply attractive at a P/E of just 10.7x [E1] and a price-to-book of 2.15x [E2], especially when paired with top-tier returns featuring an ROCE of 27.9% [E6] and an ROE of 21.8% [E7]. Furthermore, balance sheet strength is outstanding with debt-to-equity at a mere 0.06x [E32] and borrowings reduced to Rs 8 Cr [E33], while the business generated solid free cash flow of Rs 15 Cr in March 2026 [E30] and maintains a healthy dividend payout of 32% [E55].

Conceded: [E13], [E15], [E24], [E73], [E33], [E30], [E55]. The bull's reliance on recent surging profit growth [E15] and expanding margins [E24] masks a severely stagnant core business, evidenced by a sluggish 10-year sales CAGR of just 5% [E8] and a paltry 3-year sales CAGR of 4% [E10]. Furthermore, this recent profit surge rests on a declining volume base, as actual sales volumes for both gelatine and DCP fell by 5% and 8% respectively during the year [E76]. The bull highlights high ROCE [E6] and ROE [E7], but ignores the company's historical 10-year median ROE of a meager 9% [E20], proving that recent high returns are a cyclical anomaly rather than a structural baseline. Lastly, the attractive P/E of 10.7x [E1] and strong 52-week price position [E5] are counterbalanced by extreme annualised volatility of 56.7% [E47] and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -81.5% [E46], indicating the stock is a high-risk vehicle prone to catastrophic loss.

Conceded: [E8], [E10], [E20], [E76]. While the bear points to sluggish long-term sales growth [E8, E10] and volume dips [E76], it ignores that profits have dramatically outpaced top-line expansion, compounding at 39% over 5 years [E13] and 72% in the trailing twelve months [E15]. This divergence is driven by structural operational efficiency—material consumption dropped 1% and boiler efficiency reduced power and fuel costs [E73]—which has pushed operating margins up by 9 percentage points over three years to 19% [E24] in an uninterrupted 6-year increasing trend [E26]. The bear dismisses high recent ROE [E7] as a cyclical anomaly using a 10-year median [E20], yet current financial reality shows a sustained upward trajectory reaching a robust 21.8% [E7] and a median of 22% last year [E23]. Furthermore, the company generated a healthy Rs 15 Cr in free cash flow [E30] and aggressively pruned its borrowings from Rs 13 Cr to Rs 8 Cr [E33], achieving an almost debt-free balance sheet [E53] while supporting a reliable 32% dividend payout [E55]. Finally, while historical volatility [E47] and drawdowns [E46] are facts of the past, the present valuation trades at a modest 10.7x P/E [E1] despite fundamental operating strength that commands a top-tier relative strength rating of 100 [E44].

Conceded: [E13], [E15], [E24]. The bull emphasizes rapid recent profit growth and surging operating margins, but ignores that this profit surge rests on a stagnant top line, with 3-year compounded sales growth at a meager 4% [E10] and 10-year sales growth at just 5% [E8]. Furthermore, reliance on temporary margin expansions from falling coal prices and efficiency tweaks [E73] is fragile, especially when actual sales volumes for gelatine and DCP declined by 5% and 8% respectively [E76]. The bull points to a healthy 21.8% ROE [E7] while overlooking the multi-year reality: the 10-year median ROE languishes at a poor 9% [E20]. The bull celebrates low debt [E53], but promoter holding has quietly slipped from 77.65% to 75.00% [E35], and the core business faces severe structural hurdles including an industry market growth projection of only 2 to 3% [E69], acute raw material sourcing concerns for crushed bones [E78], and existential threats from cheap Chinese industrial imports [E79] and rising plant-based substitutes [E77].
